articles.title_en: Premier League Clubs Warn of Political Interference in Manchester City Appeal.
articles.title_ru: Клубы Премьер-лиги опасаются политического вмешательства в апелляцию «Манчестер Сити».
articles.preview_en: Premier League clubs say they are concerned about political interference in Manchester City's appeal after comments from Andy Burnham.
articles.preview_ru: Клубы Премьер-лиги заявили, что их беспокоит политическое вмешательство в апелляцию «Манчестер Сити» после комментариев Энди Бёрнхэма.
articles.full_en: Premier League clubs have voiced alarm over what they perceive as political meddling in Manchester City's ongoing appeal. The clubs pointed to recent remarks by Prime Minister Andy Burnham that they interpret as an attempt to influence the disciplinary process. Manchester City is contesting a points deduction imposed by the league for alleged breaches of financial regulations. Such political pressure could reshape how football governance interacts with government officials. Other Premier League teams fear that similar interventions could affect future rulings on financial fair play and club licensing. The clubs have called for an independent review of the appeal process to safeguard the sport's integrity. The dispute underscores the fragile balance between sport autonomy and governmental influence in English football.
articles.full_ru: Клубы Премьер-лиги выразили тревогу по поводу возможного политического вмешательства в апелляцию «Манчестер Сити». Клубы сослались на недавние заявления премьер-министра Энди Бёрнхэма, которые они считают попыткой повлиять на дисциплинарный процесс. «Манчестер Сити» оспаривает наложенный на него штрафные очки за предполагаемые нарушения финансовых правил. Политическое давление может изменить результат и создать прецедент для взаимодействия футбольных органов с государственными структурами. Другие команды Премьер-лиги опасаются, что аналогичные вмешательства могут затронуть будущие решения по финансовому честному игровому процессу и лицензированию клубов. Клубы потребовали независимого пересмотра процедуры апелляции, чтобы защитить целостность спорта. Этот конфликт подчеркивает хрупкий баланс между автономией футбола и влиянием государства в английском футболе.
articles.meta_en: Premier League clubs warn of political interference in Manchester City appeal, citing Andy Burnham's remarks and calling for an independent review.

articles.title_ru: Lourdes gets a Vegas glow-up at Dublin theatre festival, where canvases are slashed
articles.preview_en: A musical about a drama group’s pilgrimage and reflections on activist art join an intriguing show about lost languages In a Dublin theatre festival programme tackling heavy themes of racism, conflict
articles.preview_ru: A musical about a drama group’s pilgrimage and reflections on activist art join an intriguing show about lost languages In a Dublin theatre festival programme tackling heavy themes of racism, conflict
articles.full_en: A musical about a drama group’s pilgrimage and reflections on activist art join an intriguing show about lost languages In a Dublin theatre festival programme tackling heavy themes of racism, conflict and prejudice, Lourdes! The Musical (★★★★☆) promises something effervescent. Xnthony Ltd, the creators of Oliver Cromwell Is Really Very Sorry, have turned their lightly quizzical gaze to the French pilgrimage town – “a holy Blackpool, a divine Las Vegas” and a site of hope or desperation for five unlikely travelling companions. Back in his home village in “Countryland”, in 2008, following a diagnosis of HIV that punctures his dreams of Los Angeles, singer-songwriter Matthew (Riain Cash) lends his star power to a parish drama group taking a musical about Saint Bernadette to Lourdes. Interweaving this show-within-a-show and the pilgrimage strands, Xnthony’s lyrics and Matthew Floyd Jones’s score blend pop, club beats and soulful ballads. Directed by Sarah Meadows, the supercharged ensemble joining Cash as, variously, a droll priest (Iestyn Arwel), a terminally ill mother and her transgender daughter (Nichola MacEvilly and Danielle James) and an eager tour manager (Molly Lynch) carry the music’s tonal shifts effortlessly.
